Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:28: And therefore a voice goes forth every night, when the Holy One, blessed be He, descends into the Garden of Eden, where souls ascend before Him, and that voice says "call out" - as it is written (Isaiah 40:6), "a voice says, call out" - go and tell them to strive in Torah to join the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, along the lines of David, who said (Psalms 132:4), "I will not give sleep to my eyes, nor slumber to my eyelids, until I find a place for the LORD" - and he would strive in Torah to join the Mother, of whom it is said (Proverbs 1:8), "and do not forsake the Torah of your mother," with her husband - for the Shechinah, from the side of Chesed, is called "acts of loving-kindness," and from the side of Gevurah is called "binding" and "offering," and from the side of the central pillar is called "Torah" - and there is none to arouse her, in these attributes, toward her husband - this is what is written (Isaiah 51:18), "there is none to guide her," and so on - and therefore the voice says, "what shall I call out? All flesh is grass" - for they strive only to slaughter flesh, and these are the unlearned people [amei ha'aretz].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:29: And these who strive in acts of loving-kindness and in Torah, but strive only for themselves, of them it is said (Isaiah 40:6), "and all his kindness [chasdo] is like the flower of the field" - and all these who do not strive in it for its own sake, the holy spirit, which is the Shechinah, does not rest upon them - this is what is written (Psalms 78:39), "and He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes and does not return," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:30: Behold, it is explained how great is the obligation upon Torah students, that their intent be to unify the Shechinah, and their intent should not be for their own benefit, to attain wisdom or the reward of the World to Come - for concerning this the Shechinah complains and says, "and all his kindness is like the flower of the field," as it says, "and these who strive in acts of loving-kindness and in Torah strive only for themselves."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:31: And everything is included in a person striving to be called a son and not a servant - for a son, without qualification, serves on condition of not receiving a reward, and one who serves in order to receive a reward is punished; and it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 73b), in these words: fear and love in order to receive a reward is a maidservant - "and under three things the earth trembles," and so on, "under a servant when he becomes king, and a maidservant when she inherits her mistress" (Proverbs 30:23).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:32: Further, in the Tikkunim (page 14b), concerning the obligation of the Oral Torah to unify, in these words: happy are those who strive with the Shechinah, who is above them all, in halachah, to bring her out from exile, of whom it is said (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother is sent away," and to go to her husband, to be received in his arms, to fulfill in her (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head," and so on - for in exile, the "second," who is Metatron, rules in exile, and he is second to the King; in the place where the Matronita sits, the "second" [now] sits - and this is "and a maidservant when she inherits her mistress." And in the days of Moses, the maidservant did not rule, but the Matronita; after Moses died and Joshua, who is a "youth," inherited in the place of kingship, the maidservant ruled - as it says (Joshua 5:14), "I am the captain of the host of the LORD; now I have come" - and this has already been established - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:33: And concerning the warning to occupy oneself with Torah, we are commanded in the passage "and you shall love" (Deuteronomy 6:6), "and these words which I command you today shall be upon your heart" - behold, they shall be upon his heart - meaning, that he occupy himself with them from the heart and soul. "And you shall teach them diligently to your children" - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain that words of Torah should be sharpened in your mouth. And it says afterward, "and you shall speak of them" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Yoma 19b), "and you shall speak of them" - make them fixed. "When you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up" - behold, four times for the occupation with Torah, so that he is never free from words of Torah, even for one hour - and just as the Torah is a tree of life, and is the essence of cleaving, to cleave to the supernal life - as explained at the beginning of Parashat Va'etchanan (Zohar, page 260a): the counsel for a person in this world, who wishes to strive in Torah, is day and night, and not to depart from it - this is what is written (Joshua 1:8), "and you shall meditate on it day and night" - woe to one who departs from Torah, or separates from it, as though he departed and separated from life - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:34: And also, through the occupation with Torah, the Shechinah is unified above, and through her, unity and love are aroused between her and the Holy One, blessed be He - and the occupation with Torah is the essence of the arousal of "female waters," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 22a), in these words: come and see, the secret of the matter: the Community of Israel does not stand before the King except through Torah - for all the while Israel, on earth, strive in Torah, the Community of Israel rests with them; when they cease from words of Torah, she cannot remain with them for even one hour. Therefore, at the hour the Community of Israel is aroused toward the King, her strength grows firm, and the holy King rejoices to receive them; but whenever the Community of Israel comes to the King and Torah is not found with her, as it were, her strength weakens - woe to those who weaken the strength above! Therefore happy are those who strive in Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:35: And along these lines, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, page 268a), on the verse (Deuteronomy 30:20), "for He is your life and the length of your days, to dwell upon the land" - it explains there that the Shechinah does not stand and settle, whether above or below, except through the occupation with Torah. And it says: I found this secret in the book of Rav Hamnuna Sava, and he established the verse in the secret of the Community of Israel, as it is written (Exodus 21:10), "her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish" - and if these are withheld from her, what is written (ibid. 21:11)? "Then she shall go out for nothing, without payment" - along the lines of (Isaiah 50:1), "where is the bill of your mother's divorce, whom I have sent away?" And it is written (ibid. 52:3), "you were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without money" - and whoever withholds Torah from himself is like one who takes a man's wife and withholds her from him, for she is left like a widow who is not a widow - this is what is written (Lamentations 1:1), "she has become like a widow" - and not a widow - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:36: Behold, it is explicit that the Torah has three virtues that the other commandments do not have, namely "her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights" - and this is what he says, that whoever withholds Torah is like one who takes a man's wife - for he separates her husband from her, since the husband gives his wife food, clothing, and conjugal rights - and "conjugal rights," which is the distress of the body, is the greatest of all - and therefore the Shechinah is repaired through Torah more than through all the commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:37: And the study of Torah is [itself] one of the commandments of the Torah, except that it is comprehensive and is the most inward of all the rest - for study leads to the deed that fulfills all the other commandments, and if there is no study there is no deed, as they elaborate in the Sifrei, and we will copy their words in the coming Gate, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:1: Since, in the previous chapter, we explained that a person is obligated to unify the Shechinah always, in all his matters, as it is said (Proverbs 3:6), "in all your ways know Him" - we wish, in this chapter, to explain further several particulars a person is obligated to perform for the love of the Shechinah, and through this the Shechinah will have some rest, finding a place in which to dwell. We have already copied above, in the previous chapter, the discourse of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that all six weekdays she goes wandering from place to place, from location to location, to see whether she finds a righteous man to whom she may cleave.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:2: And when a person does all his affairs for the repair of the Shechinah, who is his mother, he is found to be a son who gives contentment to his mother, and this is the level of the masters of Kabbalah, of whom it is said (Deuteronomy 22:6), "you shall not take the mother with the children" - and they explain in the Tikkunim that the intent is, do not remove the Shechinah from over the children, for the Shechinah is always with them. And in these words (page 4a): eggs [belong to] masters of Scripture, chicks [belong to] masters of Mishnah, children [belong to] masters of Kabbalah - and of them it is said (Deuteronomy 22:6), "and the mother sitting upon the young or upon the eggs" - "you shall in any case let go" of them; but concerning the masters of Kabbalah it is said, "you shall not take the mother with the children" - for there is no discernment to recognize the Shechinah like these masters of Kabbalah, and these make for Him a dwelling, for the Holy One, blessed be He, and fly with her wherever she flies - they all wander with her in her sending away; but the chicks do not have complete wings with which to fly, which are the positive commandments, and all the more so the eggs - and therefore it is said of them, toward the Mother, "you shall in any case let go the mother" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:3: And so he also says (Tikkunei Zohar, page 21b): but children, from the innermost parts [me'av], of whom it is said (Jeremiah 31:19), "my innermost parts yearn for him" [hamu me'ai lo] - children of love from her innermost parts - and these masters of Kabbalah, of whom it is said, "you shall not take the mother with the children," for the Mother never departs from them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:4: And the reason the Mother does not depart from them is because they know how to unify the Shechinah in their commandments, their Torah, and their deeds - and the essence of the commandment and the deed is in completing the intention; but the chicks, who are masters of Mishnah, their commandments are not complete, because of the lack of intention. It follows that the comprehensive repair for the Shechinah is intention in the commandments, in Torah, and in the other deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:5: And behold, in order to arouse the heart to love of the Holy One, blessed be He, one must remember these matters that we shall explain from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and through this his heart will be aroused to love - although we are destined to say several things that arouse love, nevertheless these pertain to the essence of the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and therefore we have seen fit to explain them here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:6: He says in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Naso, page 122a) that repentance is the Shechinah, who is the final heh - and the intent is that the final heh returns to join with yud-heh-vav. He says afterward: and this repentance is called "life," for from her come forth the sources of life, which are the souls of Israel, and she is the breath that goes out and enters a person's mouth without toil and without labor, "heh" of "when they were created" [behibaram - reading the heh as itself the creative agent] - and of her it is said (Deuteronomy 8:3), "for by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD does man live" - and she is above a person's head, of whom it is said (Numbers 12:8), "and he beholds the likeness of the LORD," "surely man walks about in a mere image [tzelem]" (Psalms 39:7) - and because she is above a person's head, a person is forbidden to walk four cubits with his head uncovered, for if she were to depart from over a person's head, life would immediately depart from him. And should you say that she thus rests upon the nations of the world as well - even though heaven and earth and all their generations were not created for them - she certainly does not rest [upon them], for Moses asked of the Holy One, blessed be He, that the Shechinah not rest upon the nations of the world, and He granted it to him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:7: And when a person considers that the Shechinah is above his head, and she is the one who gives him life, which is the soul within him, and likewise the breath through which a person exists - for it is impossible for the world to exist without breath, which is air, and were the air not blown within the wings of the lung, the heart, from the side of its fire, would burn the person, as they explain in the Tikkunim (page 28a). And through a person's drawing in the air, which is the breath of the world, he exists - and this is "for by everything that proceeds from the mouth of YHVH," which is the breath of the world, that proceeds from the mouth of YHVH, who is the Shechinah, through whom man lives. And this is the heh of "when they were created" [behibaram], for the heh is breath - for the movement of the heh in its pronunciation is soft, indicating the essence of breath - and just as the supernal heh is breath, of which it is said, "for by everything that proceeds from the mouth of YHVH does man live," meaning that through that breath the supernal Man [Adam] exists, as they explain in the Zohar (Parashat Tazria, page 47b) - so too, through the breath that proceeds from the Shechinah, the lower man exists. And therefore, since Israel's life in particular is through this breath - for the breath resting upon Israel is not the same as that resting upon the nations, as explained in the discourse - and this is "man shall live" [yichyeh ha'adam], and Israel are called "Adam" - it is fitting that one love her, to perform her will.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:8: And especially when he considers how much he has sinned and rebelled against the mouth of the Shechinah, in throwing off the yoke of her commandments, and yet she did not burn him with her judgment - as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:24), "for the LORD your God is a consuming fire" - and she is called "Tzedek," judgment that has no generosity, and yet nevertheless she flows life and breath into him - it is fitting that he perform her commandments and that the fire of her love burn in his heart, so that with his every breath he be bound to her, if possible - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain in Bereshit Rabbah (section 14), in these words: Rabbi Bisna and Rabbi Acha and Rabbi Yochanan say, in the name of Rabbi Meir: this soul fills the body, and at the hour a person sleeps, it ascends and draws for him life from above. Rabbi Levi, in the name of Rabbi Chanina, said: for every single breath a person breathes, he must praise his Creator - why? "Let every soul [breath] praise the LORD" (Psalms 150:6) - every breath shall praise the LORD.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:9: And in Midrash Rabbah, Parashat Vayikra, on the verse "and if a soul shall sin," they say, in these words: another interpretation, "if a soul shall sin" - this is what Scripture says (Ecclesiastes 6:7), "all the labor of man is for his mouth" - Rabbi Shmuel bar Ami said, whatever commandments and good deeds a person has amassed do not suffice for the breath that goes out of his mouth - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:10: Further, in Eleh HaDevarim Rabbah, on the verse "and you shall love the LORD your God" - in these words: what is "with all your heart and with all your soul"? With every single soul [breath] He created in you. Rabbi Meir said: for every single breath a person draws, he is obligated to praise his Creator - from where? As it is said, "let every soul [breath] praise the LORD" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:11: And further, they say in the Yerushalmi, chapter "Ein Omdin" (halachah 1), on the verse (Psalms 46:8), "the LORD of hosts is with us," and so on - Rabbi Yosa said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: this verse should never depart from your mouth - "the LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah." And Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan (Psalms 84:13), "O LORD of hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:12: And although there are many particular explanations of these verses, for their abundant benefit, nevertheless the general matter is that one must always place before his eyes the supernal providence - and therefore it says, this verse should never depart from your mouth: for its saying "the LORD of hosts is with us" indicates His great love for Israel, that although YHVH is called "Tzevaot" [hosts], being the prince over the supernal hosts, nevertheless His providence is with us. And further, He is a stronghold and shield to protect us from the mishaps of the world, and this is "Selah," without interruption - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Eruvin 54a), that wherever "Selah" is said, it never has interruption, as it is said (Psalms 48:9), "as we have heard, so have we seen," and so on, "forever, Selah" - and from the redundancy of the verse saying "forever, Selah," they proved that wherever "Selah" is said, it never has interruption.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:13: And even according to the words of Rabbi Abahu, who says the verse is "O LORD of hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You" - there are many virtues in the attribute of trust, and one of them is that it is impossible for a person to be cleaved to his God if he has no trust in Him; and when he truly trusts, he is certainly cleaved to YHVH and has no fear of any worldly matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:14: And so Rashbi explains in the Zohar (Parashat Va'era, page 22a), in these words: another interpretation (Isaiah 26:4), "trust in the LORD forever" - all his days, a person must be strong through the Holy One, blessed be He - for so David said (Psalms 25:2), "O my God, I trust in You; let me not be ashamed, let not my enemies triumph over me" - and whoever places his trust and strength in Him properly, none of the people of the world can harm him, for whoever places his strength in the holy Name endures in the world - why? Because the world endures through the holy Name - this is what is written, "for in Yah, the LORD, is the Rock of worlds" - He forms the worlds - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:15: And he explains two matters concerning trust: the first, that one must be constant in trust all his days - and this is precise in his saying "forever" [adei ad]. And the second, that the essence of trust is the strength of cleaving to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, "all his days a person must be strong through the Holy One, blessed be He" - and it says "to be strong" - and so too below, where it says "placed his trust and strength in Him," indicating the strength of the grip of cleaving, such that he cannot be separated from Him, and therefore he trusts in every matter and does not fear the mishaps of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:16: And the essence of cleaving is in YHVH, as explained in the discourse, which says, "because the world endures through the holy Name." And the reason is that the Name YHVH is the inner vitality both of this world and of the World to Come - for just as the soul is the life of the body, so this world is the body, and the Name YHVH is the soul within it; and were His vitality, Heaven forfend, to depart from the world, the world would remain chaos and void - for His Name, blessed be He, is the soul sustaining everything. And therefore, since a person cleaves to YHVH, who is the soul, it is fitting that he endure in the world more, because he always polishes his soul from the root of the supernal life, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the LORD your God are alive" - as I explained in the previous chapter. Behold, we have explained the reason that arouses in us love of the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:17: And the reason that arouses love of the Holy One, blessed be He, is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 134b), in these words: "from every man whose heart makes him willing you shall take My offering" (Exodus 25:2) - this verse should have said, "from every man whose heart makes him willing"; what is "from every man"? Rather, here is a secret for the masters of understanding. Happy are these righteous who know how to set their will toward the supernal, holy King, and all their will is not toward this world and the longing for its vanity, but rather they know and strive to set their will and cleave above, in order to draw the will of their Master toward them, from above to below. And from what place do they draw that will of their Master, to draw it toward them? They draw it from one supernal, holy place, from which all holy wills go forth. And who is "every man" [kol ish]? This is the righteous man, called "Kol" [All], as it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:8), "and the profit of the land is in everything [kol]" - "kol" is a king served by the field - therefore "all the commandments of everything [kol]" (Psalms 119:128) - "ish" [man], as it is said, "a righteous man" [ish tzaddik] - this is "every man," the master of the house, whose will is always toward the Matronita, like a husband who loves his wife, always making his heart willing - he loves her, and his heart, which is his Matronita, makes willing to cleave to him; and although in this great love they never separate from one another, from this "every man, master of the house" - "you shall take My offering." The way of the world is that whoever wishes to take a man's wife from him, he is jealous and does not allow it; but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so - although all her love is toward Him and His love toward her, from Him they take her, to make her dwell among them - from that supernal place where all the love between a woman and her husband rests, "you shall take My offering." Happy is the portion of Israel, and happy are all who merit this - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:18: And further on it says: happy is their portion, for although they take her here, they can do so only with the permission of her husband and with her own permission, and to perform the service of love toward Him - and then, through His love, "you shall take My offering" - and all this in those services of prayer and repair that Israel arrange every day - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:19: Our intent is explained in this discourse: that although the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes for the love of His Shechinah, nevertheless, out of His love for Israel, He gives us permission to draw her to ourselves below, through prayer and commandments, so that through them she be unified above - and we arouse the love from her toward Him, along the lines of "who chooses His people Israel in love," explained above - and this is what it says, "to perform the service of love toward Him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:20: Indeed, the discourse has matters requiring examination that are not relevant here to this exposition; and what is relevant to the exposition of cleaving and love that we are engaged in is explained in the discourse, which speaks of the virtue of the righteous who know how to strip their thought of physicality and cleave their thought and will to the King of kings of kings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:21: And these words of his may be understood through what he says in Parashat Bereshit (Zohar, Bereshit, Heichal Kodesh Kodashim, page 45b), where he mentions the matter of the wills revealed at the time of the supernal union; see there. And all the wills are revealed through the righteous man, who is the one who unites - and there is the essential cleaving of the soul of the lower righteous man, as it says: and then that will of everything is sweetened, and is not grasped within, within concealment; and then happy is the portion of one who cleaves to his Master at that hour - happy is he above, happy is he below; of him it is written (Proverbs 23:25), "let your father and your mother be glad, and let her who bore you rejoice."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:22: And it further says on: whoever merits to cleave to his Master in this manner inherits all the worlds, love above, love below - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:23: And through this we may understand its saying, "his heart, who is his Matronita, makes willing to cleave to him" - because through him the supernal will is revealed to her, as explained, and she shines with the light of the Infinite, and this is the reality of the union; and it is his love toward her, in the secret of "and a river went out of Eden to water the garden" - and if there is no garden, where would the river's flowing and watering go? And this is what my teacher, peace be upon him, explains in Sefer HaPardes, that the upper ones need the lower ones. And through "you shall take My offering" and unify her in those services of prayer, you are cleaved to the supernal will revealed in unification, as explained - and through this the whole discourse is found bound together as one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:24: And we thus learn that all cleaving depends on the repairs of prayer, which are all repairs of the Shechinah and her unification; and we thus learn that the essence of cleaving and love depends on stripping the thought from the desires of this world, all of whose desires are nullified in death, as is known - and the essence is to cleave one's soul to the supernal will. And the essential thing you must know, [about] all the unifications and the whole reality of the service, is that there is no difference between us and Him, blessed be He - though He is exalted, high above the highest - He is with us, watching over the particulars that elevate to His seat, and there is no difference except from the side of sin, as it says (Isaiah 59:2), "your iniquities have made a separation," and so on. Indeed, when a person repents, he is bound with his Creator - and the proof is when you discern what we wrote in the previous chapters, of how many miracles were performed for Israel, and the Holy One, blessed be He, performs for us always, and answers us at the time of our distress.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:25: And especially when a person discerns the virtue of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and the other Tannaim, whose speech would come true immediately, and sometimes even without full intention, along the lines of "an unwitting error that goes forth from before the ruler," and so on, mentioned several times in the Gemara (Mo'ed Katan 18a), and in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (page 218a), "Master of the universe, Rabbi Yitzchak has become known to us" - and several such miracles brought in the book of the Zohar - therefore, when a person considers this matter, he will see that there is no screen at all between him and holiness, and therefore he is obligated to serve the Creator like one who serves a king standing before him and performs the supernal will according to the changes in the orders of the supernal governance in the times of day and night and the other times - so he should perform his service in his prayer and his Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:26: First, it is fitting that a person direct his whole intent every day to unify the Shechinah in the three prayers, Shacharit, Mincha, and Ma'ariv - and the reason for these three times is that according to the change of the lower time, the supernal governance changes to Chesed, to judgment, and to mercy - and therefore in the morning we arouse Chesed. And along these lines, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain in Bereshit Rabbah, Parashat Vayetze (68:9), the reason for the three prayers; it says there: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, the fathers instituted the three prayers - Abraham instituted the morning prayer, and so on. And it further says: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said, corresponding to the three times the day changes: in the evening, one should say, "may it be Your will, O LORD my God, that You bring me out from darkness to light"; in the morning, one must say, "I give thanks before You, O LORD my God, that You have brought me out from darkness to light"; at Mincha, one should say, "may it be Your will, O LORD my God, just as You have granted me to see the sun in its rising, so may You grant me to see it in its setting." The Rabbis say: they instituted them corresponding to the daily offerings - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:27: If so, it follows that according to the change of time, so the praise and thanksgiving to the Name is obligated, for the good He has done; and in order that one be complete in loving the Name and pray with the desire of the heart, remembering the good He does for him, the prayers were instituted at different times.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:28: And along these lines, it is explained in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 28:1), on (Ecclesiastes 1:5), "and the sun rises, and the sun sets" - in these words: Rabbi Levi said, whatever creatures raise up through commandments and good deeds in this world suffices for the Holy One, blessed be He, to make the sun shine for them, as it is said, "and the sun rises, and the sun sets."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:29: And at the time he awakens from his sleep, if he rises early to recite Torah for the love of the Shechinah, how good is his portion, as we shall elaborate on its virtue, with God's help. And this Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Parashat Va'era, page 30a), in these words: come and see, when the King comes to His bed, at the time midnight arrives, the north wind is aroused, which arouses affection toward the Matronita - for were it not for the arousal of the north, the King would not unite with her, because affection begins in the north, as it is said (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head," and the south embraces in love, as it is written, "and his right hand embraces me." Then how many joyful ones arouse song until morning comes, as it is written (Job 38:7), "when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy." And when morning comes, all the upper and lower ones say song, and Israel correspondingly below, as it is written (Isaiah 62:6), "you who remind the LORD, take no rest [al domi lachem]" - "take no rest" precisely at night: when midnight arrives, those whose desire is to remember the Holy One, blessed be He, continually, give their heart no rest, and stand to remember the Holy One, blessed be He; when morning arrives, they hasten to the synagogue and praise the Holy One, blessed be He; and so too after midday, and so too at night, when it grows dark and night cleaves to darkness and the daughter of the sun [the moon] - of these it is written, "you who remind the LORD, take no rest" - and this is the holy people of Israel - to this point.
